H4.verdict: BETTER than r7 (and r8) for a manager
H4.why: Safety items the numeric budget had squeezed out are back: kill switch and drill, reconciliation drill, a real booking-API staging journey, the pilot-salon gate, the pass bar and the call-cap test. All waits are modelled on day 1, the summary is exact, every alternative reproduces, and the plan is back on 5 focused h/day with a sensitivity row. Defects fell from 11 to 7. The cost is length: design+plan is +45 % (7,256 vs 4,994) and tickets +38 %. About 11 % of design+plan is waste by the rule (812 words) plus 265 words of permitted run history. Of the growth, about three-quarters is substance: restored floor items, guarantees, failure rows and data/security tables. The rest is restatement, plus decision and ticket-scope cells written at production granularity for a two-week MVP. Three failure rows are still missing (cancel-all, partial move, read fails). One unmodelled dependency (G07 needs G06) turns 'fits' into 'low end only' if taken literally

H5.verdict: SAME (slightly better on structure, with one new high-impact gap)
H5.why: Design+plan is 3 % shorter, and handoffs, the legal wait, the DPIA gate and the telemetry row are fixed. The summary and what-ifs reproduce. But the AI-notice test is still missing. The 'fits at 95 of 100' headline rests on W1 (DPIA) not waiting for G12's data-flow evidence, which the tickets say it needs: modelled, GA slips to about day 120. The G26 ramp has no calendar days, and the portal wait was dropped. Tickets grew 34 %, mostly more specific scope and acceptance (substance) plus ~590 words of new pointer and skills boilerplate

P5_verdict.overall: The rule did what it was meant to do: substance came back (H4 most visibly) and no floor item was cut to save words. Length went up in H4, not down. Measured waste is about 7-8 % of all words (10-11 % of design+plan), so the extra length is mostly substance, but the documents are long for an MVP manager (H4 design 4,354 words). The remaining failures are schedule-modelling escapes, not length: prose dependencies and calendar time that are not in the yaml

top_issues: Prose-to-schedule escapes remain the main defect class and can flip the headline: H4 G07 needs G06 (10.13); H5 W1 needs G12 (120 days); H5 G26 ramp days (101)
Approvals and third-party waits are still unmodelled: H4 deployment and go-live approvals; H5 Guidewire production client, portal release, claims-team inputs
Failure rows lost silently between rounds: H4 cancel-all, partial move, read-fails, token-expiry (back in r8, gone again); H5 AI-notice acceptance

Waste is concentrated in restated tables: scope-gate tables restating A-rows, deferred-control tables repeating the depth table, person tables restating yaml, guarantee cells restating tests, and H5's 27 pointer sentences
No length ceiling means H4's design doubled toward production granularity; the rule's 'design at the profile's depth' clause is not yet biting
